verdict.headline: Long-term bond yields sit near 2002 highs as a week of inflation tests begins
verdict.label: Weekend: S&P 500 closed Fri at 7,722.72 (+0.73%, week -0.3%), Nasdaq 27,190.86 (+1.19%, week +0.5%); 10Y 5.281%, 30Y 5.629% (2002 high 5.644%); Oct hike odds ~20%; Aug core PCE 3.0% y/y, 2.0% 3-month annualized; BTC ~$84,800 Sat evening, flat on the day.
verdict.rationale_short:
What happened: no stock or bond market traded today. Markets closed Friday with the S&P 500 at 7,722.72, down about 0.3% on the week, and the Nasdaq up about 0.5%. Over the week, CME FedWatch odds of an October 28 hike fell from about 76% to about 20% after September payrolls rose only 29,000. Long yields rose anyway: the ten-year ended at 5.281% and the thirty-year at 5.629%, 1.5 basis points under its 2002 high. Bitcoin, the one market open, held near $84,800 through Saturday in a range of about $500.

What it means: two readings of inflation now point different ways. August core PCE was 3.0% from a year earlier, but its three-month annualized pace slowed to 2.0%, the Fed's target. Against that, ISM manufacturing prices paid jumped to 77.9 and Brent is still near $102 with the Strait of Hormuz disrupted. Long yields rising while hike odds fell suggests investors are asking more to hold long-term bonds for reasons beyond the Fed's next move, such as inflation risk, deficits and bond supply; one week cannot prove which.

What would change the picture: a thirty-year close above 5.644% would put long yields at their highest since 2002; a close under 5.44% would say the rise is fading. Sunday's OPEC+ meeting, expected to hold November targets, Monday's ISM services prices index and Wednesday's minutes of the September hike are the tests. Conviction is low: no market traded today, and the news sites this run tried to read were blocked, so weekend developments, including reports of further tanker attacks near Hormuz, could not be checked.
verdict.lede_short: Markets enter the week with the 30-year Treasury yield at 5.629%, just under its 2002 high, even though weak hiring cut October hike odds to about 20%. Inflation signals conflict: core PCE slowed to a 2.0% three-month pace, but factory prices paid jumped to 77.9 and Brent sits near $102. Monday's ISM services prices index is the first test; a 30-year close above 5.644% would resume the rise.

supporting_data.label: The thirty-year Treasury yield closed Friday at 5.629%, 1.5 basis points under its 2002 high, after rising about 14 basis points on the week — long yields climbed in the same week hike odds fell, so the Fed path is not what is driving them.
CME FedWatch odds of an October 28 hike stood near 20% at Friday's close, down from about 76% a week earlier — the market has largely stopped expecting an October move.
August core PCE prices rose 3.0% from a year earlier, but the three-month annualized pace slowed to 2.0% — recent months are running at the Fed's target even though the yearly figure is not.

ISM services for September is due Monday, expected near 55.1 against 55.4, with minutes of the September hike on Wednesday — its prices index will show whether manufacturing's jump to 77.9 is spreading to services.
OPEC+ meets online Sunday and is expected to leave November output targets unchanged — that adds no planned supply, and actual output already runs below target.
Bitcoin traded near $84,800 Saturday evening, up 0.2% in 24 hours in an $84,507-$85,031 range — the one market open this weekend is steady after slipping from above $87,000 on Friday.

watchlist_mentions.note: Closed Friday at $233.95, up 1.34%, after its first record intraday high since May; chips led the Nasdaq-100 to a record as hike odds fell.
Rose about 5% Friday after third-quarter deliveries of 486,532 beat the 461,974 consensus; results due October 21.
PepsiCo reports this week, one of the few large earnings reports before the season starts the following week.
Near $84,800 Saturday evening, up 0.2% in 24 hours in a narrow $84,507-$85,031 range.

trade_setups.thesis: The thirty-year rose about 14 basis points last week to 5.629% while October hike odds fell from about 76% to about 20%, so the long-end pressure is coming from outside the Fed path; it sits 1.5 basis points under its 2002 high.
trade_setups.entry: Thirty-year 5.629% between the 2002 high of 5.644% above and 5.44% below.
trade_setups.invalidation: A close above 5.644% would resume the rise; a close under 5.44% would say last week's rise was positioning.

trade_setups.asset: ISM services prices against December hike odds
trade_setups.thesis: Core PCE slowed to a 2.0% three-month pace while manufacturing prices paid reached 77.9; Monday's services prices index shows which signal is spreading.
trade_setups.entry: ISM services expected near 55.1 against 55.4 prior; manufacturing prices paid 77.9.
trade_setups.invalidation: A soft services prices index alongside weak payrolls would weaken the case for any further hike; a jump like manufacturing's would keep it alive.

trade_setups.thesis: Brent ended the week at $102.25 with Hormuz shipping disrupted; OPEC+ is expected to hold November targets on Sunday, adding no planned supply.
trade_setups.invalidation: An unexpected OPEC+ output increase, or confirmed new tanker attacks over the weekend, would move oil at Sunday evening's futures open.
